displayedInputs.question: A student wants to find out how much time residents across a city spend reading each day. The student randomly stops 100 readers at a library entrance to survey them. The main problem with this survey is

choices.A: The sample size is too large
choices.B: People sampled at a library entrance may read more than other residents, so the survey may overestimate reading time and lacks representativeness
choices.C: There is no problem because the people were stopped randomly
choices.D: Only elderly people should be surveyed

displayedInputs.question: Which of the following statements about sample representativeness is correct?

choices.A: As long as the sample is randomly selected from the population and its size is appropriate, it can reflect the population reasonably well
choices.B: The larger the sample size, the more representative the sample must be, regardless of the selection method
choices.C: Selecting only acquaintances makes the sample more convenient and more representative
